Operator: Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Insurance Group Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. Instructions for queuing your questions will be provided at that time. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Lisa Chen, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Thank you, Operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to Apex Insurance Group's Q2 2024 earnings call. Joining me on the call today are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Rodriguez, Chief Financial Officer; David Patel, Chief Underwriting Officer; and Emily Wong, Chief Investment Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that some of the statements we are making today may be considered forward-looking. These statements are subject to certain risks and uncertainties that could cause our actual results to differ materially from those projected. We encourage you to review our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks and uncertainties.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson: Thank you, Lisa, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on Apex Insurance Group's performance for Q2 2024. We delivered strong results, driven by favorable loss ratio trends amid stable claims frequency and moderating severity, robust gross written premium growth across key lines, the positive impact of refined actuarial assumptions, disciplined pricing actions supporting premium volume, and proactive capital deployment into high-return opportunities. Our focus on precision pricing, digital underwriting, and claims optimization continues to yield positive outcomes.

Michael, our CFO, will now provide a more detailed review of our financial performance.

Michael Rodriguez: Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Our net income was $450 million, or $2.15 per share. Key drivers of our financial performance included underwriting discipline, premium expansion, and favorable reserve developments. Our combined ratio was 92.4%, reflecting effective underwriting and claims management. Investment income for the quarter was $320 million. We continue to maintain a strong capital position, with our group-wide RBC ratio at 620%.

Turning now to our underwriting performance, I'd like to focus particularly on loss ratio trends and their primary drivers—claims frequency and severity—across our core lines of business. As everyone knows, the loss ratio, calculated as incurred losses and loss adjustment expenses divided by earned premiums, is essential for evaluating our capacity to price risks profitably in the current environment. In Q2, we achieved a consolidated loss ratio of 62.3%, improving 620 basis points year-over-year from 68.5% in Q2 2023, and 180 basis points ahead of our full-year 2023 average of 64.1%. This is our strongest quarterly loss ratio since Q1 2021, before the escalation in catastrophe activity and inflation pressures.

Excluding catastrophe losses, which came in at $145 million mainly from severe convective storms in the Midwest and Southeast U.S., our ex-cat loss ratio was 59.8%, down from 65.2% last year. This improvement stems from consistent pricing discipline, better risk selection, and initial gains from our multi-year technical programs. The combined ratio of 92.4%—comfortably under our under-95% target—produced roughly $250 million in pre-tax underwriting income this quarter.

Let's unpack the main drivers: claims frequency and severity.

On claims frequency, measured as claims per exposure unit—like per insured vehicle in personal auto or per $100 of payroll in workers' comp—it held mostly steady quarter-over-quarter but rose modestly 2.1% year-over-year overall. In personal auto, our biggest line at 42% of net earned premiums, frequency increased 3.4% YoY to 7.8 claims per 100 car years, influenced by distracted driving and higher post-pandemic vehicle miles traveled, reaching 1.05 trillion VMT in the U.S. according to DOT figures. This aligns with industry patterns, as companies like Progressive and Geico have noted comparable rises amid reduced commercial fleet usage.

We've managed this effectively via our ZenithDrive telematics program, now covering 28% of auto policyholders, up from 18% a year ago. Using GPS and accelerometer data, we've cut frequency by 15% for users through tailored usage-based insurance pricing that adjusts premiums dynamically based on behaviors like hard braking or nighttime driving. In commercial auto, frequency stayed flat at 4.2 claims per 100 vehicles, supported by AI-driven fleet monitoring with partners like Samsara.

Property lines experienced a slight 1.2% YoY frequency drop to 1.1 claims per $1,000 of insured value, due to calmer weather outside cat events and our roof age limits—now restricting standard homeowners policies to 20 years or less in high-risk areas like Florida and Texas.

Severity, or average cost per claim, has been more challenging, but we're observing notable moderation. Overall severity increased just 4.8% YoY to $2,450 per claim, far below the 11.2% industry average from ISO in 2023. Personal auto severity eased to a 5.9% YoY rise at $4,120 per claim, down from prior double-digit growth. Used parts inflation slowed to 3.2% from 8.5%, per CCC Intelligent Solutions, and labor rates stabilized near $52 per hour after hitting $55. In no-fault states like Michigan, medical severity grew 7.1% YoY from attendant care, but shifting to MedPay endorsements has limited our exposure.

Workers' comp severity rose 6.3% YoY to $42,000 per lost-time claim, driven by 5.8% medical trends matching NCCI estimates and wage inflation on indemnity. Our virtual rehab network with Optum has lowered severity by 8% for participants by speeding return-to-work.

Ex-cat property severity climbed 3.7% to $18,500 per claim, tempered by reinsurance that caps our net retention on wind/hail at $10 million per event.

Regionally, U.S. operations, 72% of premiums, led with a loss ratio of 61.5%, up from 64.8% YoY, backed by 9.2% earned premium growth from 7.8% average rate hikes, consistent with A.M. Best industry data. California personal lines stayed at 60.2% post-Prop 103 approvals, while Florida home faced 12% severity pressure after Hurricane Idalia remnants, countered by 15% rates and non-renewal of 5,000 coastal policies.

Europe, 18% of premiums, improved to 65.1% from 70.3%, helped by mild weather and AXA XL facultative reinsurance on D&O. UK motor frequency fell 1.5% with better road safety, though severity rose 6% from parts issues. Asia-Pacific, 10%, held at 63.4%, with Japan property gaining from earthquake retrofits cutting severity 4%.

These results reflect our three-pillar approach: precision pricing, digital underwriting, and claims optimization. Our GLMs with LexisNexis and Verisk data update weekly, capturing 2-3 loss ratio points per cycle. Generative AI in claims triage has reduced cycle times 22% and boosted fraud detection 14%, saving $35 million yearly.

For Q3, we see ex-cat loss ratios in the low 60s, full-year 62-64% assuming 3 points of normalized cats. Risks like medical inflation and EV repair costs—up 20% per Audatex—persist, but auto rate adequacy at 105% indicated and our $500 million reinsurance renewal with QS at $150 million attachment give us strength. We're targeting mid-teens ROEs cycle-wide, ahead of Travelers and Chubb ex-cat.

Before moving on, another key factor in our results was changes in our actuarial assumptions and their financial impact. Actuarial assumptions form the foundation of our liability valuations in life & annuity, group health, and P&C segments. We update them rigorously using emerging data, peer benchmarks, macro shifts, and regs like LDTI under U.S. GAAP and IFRS 17.

In Q2, we booked a net $285 million favorable impact from these updates, adding about 15 basis points to core ROE. This came from mortality, lapse, discount rate, and longevity tweaks, partly offset by group health morbidity. Let's detail it.

Mortality drove the biggest piece, $180 million favorable. Our 2023-2024 studies on 2.5 million lives showed rates 4-6% below priors, matching Prudential and MetLife trends as COVID excess mortality normalizes to SOA's 2023 VBT at 95% confidence.

In individual life, we cut base mortality 2.5% for ages 65-80 on better healthcare and vaccines, freeing $120 million term reserves. Annuities saw 1.8% off loaded factors for FIAs (25% of $45 billion block), yielding $60 million.

U.S.-heavy (85%), Europe under Solvency II had prior updates via EIOPA tests. Asia with Manulife JVs held steady on longevity. Our Palantir-powered Actuarial Data Hub with ML segments by comorbidities and wearables, cutting uncertainty 12%.

Lapse assumptions added $65 million favorable as behavior proved stickier, surrenders 8% below VA projections like Lincoln National.

Fed terminal at 4.75-5.00% narrowed FIA crediting (4.2%) to CDs; lapses down 1.2 points for VAs. Unemployment 4.1%, net worth +7% suppressed them; partial withdrawals down 15% for 55+. EMEA group life lapses up 0.5 point ($10 million unfavorable) from UK pressures.

Our Dynamic Lapse Hedging with equity options cuts basis risk 20%.

Discount rates unlocked $75 million with Treasury steepening (10-year +45 bps to 4.35%) and spreads -12 bps. Life reserves blended rate to 4.2% (AA minus 50 bps premium). P&C cat reserves +25 bps per NAIC for wildfires.

Europe IFRS 17 milder +15 bps; Japan flat, hedged with swaps. Stochastic generator on 5,000 SOFR paths robust.

Longevity neutral -$15 million, +0.3 years U.S. annuitants from CMS GLP-1 data like Athene. Group health -$20 million unfavorable, +5.2% severity from behavioral/GLP-1, +3% incidence for stop-loss over 85% MLR.

U.S. (70% reserves) $210 million favorable via LDTI; Europe +$35 million MA expansion; APAC +$25 million India/Australia; LatAm neutral.

Annual studies, CAS peers, KPMG audits ensure discipline. FY2025 $100-150 million tailwinds from mortality/Fed cuts. Risks longevity (120% CMxL), cat inflation; $500 million Swiss Re tower.

Pivoting to RILAs (15% VA sales), AI Actuarial Twin cuts EVBoA volatility 25%. This bolsters 12.5% ROE, $2.1 billion CR target.

Shifting to gross written premiums, which rose 9.2% YoY to $14.8 billion—eighth straight double-digit constant currency quarter. Organic 10.7% ex-FX headwinds (USD strength -1.5% Europe). Retention >91%, new wins high-margin. Book yield 82% pre-hurricane reinsurance.

Personal Lines +11.4% to $6.2 billion: 7% rate, 4.4% volume. Hardening market +9-10% industry rates.

Auto +13.2% $3.9 billion: 8.5 points rate on 15% repairs/ social inflation; +4.7% volume Telematics (2.5M policies, +18% conversion); retention 92.5% fintech like Klarna. SE U.S. 40% new post-Idalia; CA +6% non-renew 15k wildfire.

Home +8.1% $2.3B: 6.2 points rate storms; +1.9% volume bundles 68%. RMS modeling flat ceded; FL flat ex-rate SB 2-A; TX/Midwest hail; UK +12% parametric.

Commercial +6.8% $5.1B: 5% rate, 1.8% volume vs. 95% CR industry. Exit CA small auto.

Workers' comp +9.5% $1.8B: +7% rates wage 4.2%; wearables -12% freq, +15% wins.

GL/Umbrella +5.2% $1.7B: social inflation; excess +22% D&O.

Comm auto/property flat+2% $1.6B: property +8% wildfires, -3% fleets; APAC JV $150M.

Specialty/L&H +14.7% $3.5B sub-60% LR.

Cyber/Tech E&O +22% $1.1B: +15% post-outages; CyberGuard IBM +25% EMEA share; U.S. +30%.

D&O +12% $900M: Side A +28% Swiss Re.

L&H +10.2% $1.5B: stop-loss +16% 7.5% trends; voluntary 1M lives LatAm.

Regions: NA 75% +10%; $500M InsurTech. EMEA 15% +8% FCA/Hannover. APAC/LatAm 10% +20% blockchain parametric.

Optimize to 25/40/35 mix; divest $400M crop. AI underwriting -40% cycles. FY24 9-11% GWP.

On capital deployment, with equity $28.5B +8% YoY, RBC 620%>500%, Solvency II 180%. Excess $4.2B post-$1.8B reinsurance/$ capex.

Prioritize organic, bolt-ons P&C/group life, products, returns. Mid-teens ROE, 10-15% EPS acc.

Acquisitions: $1.1B YTD, pipeline $2-3B. CyberShield Re $850M Q4 close: $400M GWP 88% CR ML tail; $60M synergies 12% acc2025. SingaLife 75% $450M: 1.2M lives $320M EV 15% CAGR health. U.S. tuck-ins workers' comp.

Products: $750M R&D +30%. ClimateGuard parametric $500M 55-60% LR Swiss Re. VitalLink wearables UK/Aus RL fraud $45M Q2. ESG riders 7% credits 92% ret.

Tech: $300M AWS/Snowflake Touchstone; blockchain Chainlink -14 days CA; genAI IFRS17 -20% exp 28%.

Regions: NA 60%, APAC 15%, Europe 20%, LatAm 5%. Hedge 3.1% inflation +6.2% ex-cat rates; $20B FI 4.8% dur 5.2.

Returns: Div +10% $0.65 2.8%; $1.5B buyback $600M 12x.

Drive 8-10% GWP CAGR $52B2026 ROE16%; 12% IRR.

Finally, the impact of pricing changes on premium volume. Prioritizing adequacy over volume in hardening P&C, inflation repairs/med/reins.

Personal 55% $4.2B NWP: +6.2% renewals loss trends; auto CR98.5% telematics 28% 15% disc. Renewal vol +3.1% ret87.2%; new flat $450M tight FL/CA BI+12%. Overall +2.8% $4.25B yield5.4%. Midwest/SE +4.5%; CA -1.2% QS.

Commercial 30% $2.3B: vol+5.6% $2.42B +7.8% mid-market LR62.3%. E&S +12.4%rates +8.2%vol vs.110% peers; ret89% new+7% cyber. Europe +6.8% Lloyd's+11%; APAC +2.1%.

Specialty 10% +4.1% $780M flat-+2.5% parametric20%; D&O55% lit db. L&H5% +1.8% $390M +4.7% med7.2%; life -0.5% EV+3.2% VUL.

Aggregate NWP $7.82B +3.7%; earned $7.65B +3.4%. +6.1% rate offset +0.2% count -2.4% expos. Ex-cat AY LR61.8% +140bps CR92.4%.

Pillars: Data ApexDrive/RiskOptix +200bps; $50M sat img 10% prec. Regions +5-7%US +8%EU LatAm micro. Reins95% stable. Q4 4-6% norm cats; weekly filings42 states.

That covers our prepared financial review.

David Patel: Thank you, Michael. I'd like to provide an update on our underwriting performance. We've seen continued strong performance in our personal auto line. We are actively managing our exposure to catastrophes and have implemented several initiatives to improve our risk selection, including enhanced telematics adoption and AI-driven modeling as Michael outlined.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator: Thank you. At this time, we will conduct a question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Mayer with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Mayer: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the loss ratio trends, particularly frequency in auto?

Sarah Thompson: Good question, John. As Michael detailed, frequency in personal auto rose modestly due to VMT rebound, but our ZenithDrive program has contained it effectively with 15% reductions for participants. We're seeing similar dynamics industry-wide.

Operator: Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter: Good morning. Could you discuss the impact of recent market conditions, like inflation, on your actuarial assumptions?

Michael Rodriguez: Thanks, Emily. Inflation has influenced morbidity slightly unfavorably in group health, but overall, higher discount rates from yield shifts more than offset, netting $285 million favorable. Our stochastic modeling keeps us robust.

Operator: Our next question comes from David Kim with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Kim: What is the expected impact of regulatory changes like LDTI on your underwriting strategy?

David Patel: Great point, David. LDTI enables smoother assumption updates, supporting our precision pricing pillar. We've already seen benefits in reserve releases without locked-in periods, aligning with our low-60s ex-cat guidance.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Grant with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Grant: On capital deployment, any updates on the CyberShield deal?

Michael Rodriguez: On track for Q4 close, Lisa. It fits perfectly, adding ML tail expertise to our cyber growth.

Operator: Seeing no further questions at this time...

Sarah Thompson: Thank you for your questions and your interest in Apex Insurance Group. In closing, we are confident in our ability to continue delivering strong results and creating value for our shareholders. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
